source_contract: Same qualified source/native binaries and captured MLP fixture as the completed three-arm cohort; no historical timing or admission pooling.
startup: Original synthetic initializer returns its generated object without clone/copy. Actual first-pass default-inclusive search and original winner/cache remain intact.

confirmation.order: Balanced six explicit-first and six default-first per process, frozen before execution.
confirmation.candidate: First minimum of the eight original explicit M144 candidates.
confirmation.decision: median(log(explicit/default))<0 selects explicit; zero selects default. No margin or rounding.
confirmation.scope: Hypothetical decision frozen before graph capture; never publish a new winner.

held_out_score.unit: Fresh process; all within-process windows retained.
held_out_score.unchanged_choice: Exactly1, even if independently captured graphs differ.

counts.corrected: Original slow and confirmed not slow.
counts.introduced: Original not slow and confirmed slow.
counts.interpretation: Directional counts use measured point estimates without a margin; not per-process significance claims. Report all unchanged, improved, adverse, and tied results.

uncertainty.unit: Complete fresh processes; shared indices across metrics.
uncertainty.interval: Exploratory95% percentile interval with type7 interpolation; eight processes on one device/fixture/time window.

review_gate.supports_focused_review: corrected>0 AND introduced=0 AND whole-process95%CI upper for confirmation/original graph ratio<1.
review_gate.otherwise: Stop this bounded checkpoint. Classify promising but inconclusive, introduced slow choices, or neutral/ineffective as appropriate.

limitations: Both decisions use the same post-confirmation graphs; this is not untouched startup versus a deployed policy.
Synthetic profiling operands and captured serving operands remain different. This does not isolate noise, input values, or measurement objective.
Capture/history effects remain possible; retain capture-order and first-position strata.
No eager performance, full-model serving, universal safety, graph-policy adoption, or managed-cache claim.
